description: "Fetching 3D conformers of small molecules from PubChem"

---

Small molecules can be fetched from [PubChem](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/) with
[](`~mn.Molecule.fetch`) and `database="pubchem"`. The code is either a compound CID or a
compound name, and the compound's 3D conformer is downloaded as an `.sdf` file, with its
hydrogens and bonds. Like other downloads, the file is cached and reused on later fetches.

## Setup

```{python}
import molecularnodes as mn

canvas = mn.Canvas(mn.scene.Cycles(samples=32), resolution=(800, 600), transparent=True)
```

## Fetch by CID or Name

A code made only of digits is a CID, anything else is looked up by name. Aspirin is CID
`2244`, so both of these fetch the same structure.

```{python}
aspirin = mn.Molecule.fetch("2244", database="pubchem")
aspirin.object.hide_render = True
aspirin = mn.Molecule.fetch("aspirin", database="pubchem")
aspirin.add_style("ball_and_stick")
canvas.look_at(aspirin, viewpoint="pca")
canvas.snapshot()
```

## Several Molecules

Each fetched molecule is its own object, so it can be moved to sit beside the others in
a grid. Combine their views with `+` to frame all of them at once.

```{python}
aspirin.object.hide_render = True

names = ["caffeine", "dopamine", "ATP", "protoporphyrin IX"]
mols = []
for i, name in enumerate(names):
    mol = mn.Molecule.fetch(name, database="pubchem")
    mol.add_style("sticks" if name == "ATP" else "ball_and_stick")
    mol.object.location = ((i % 2) * 1.9, -(i // 2) * 1.3, 0)
    mols.append(mol)

view = mols[0].get_view()
for mol in mols[1:]:
    view = view + mol.get_view()
canvas.look_at(view, viewpoint="top")
canvas.snapshot()
```

## Compounds Without a 3D Conformer

PubChem only computes 3D conformers for some compounds: not for salts, mixtures, many
metal complexes, or very large or flexible molecules. For those, the fetch raises an error
rather than falling back to a flat 2D structure. Heme is one of them, while its
metal-free ring, protoporphyrin IX, has a 3D conformer.

```{python}
from molecularnodes.download import FileDownloadPDBError

try:
    mn.Molecule.fetch("heme", database="pubchem")
except FileDownloadPDBError as e:
    print(e)
```
